use_case: A podcast's episode pipeline: guests, recordings, edits, publish dates and sponsors for a two-person B2B SaaS interview show.

guests.name: Priya Nathaniel
guests.bio: Head of Platform Engineering at a mid-size fintech; spent six years building internal developer tooling before that at two Y Combinator startups. Speaks often about golden-path platforms and the cost of bespoke CI.

guests.name: Dorian Cassell
guests.bio: Founder of a three-person devtools studio that ships a popular open-source feature-flag library. Previously led growth engineering at a logistics marketplace.

guests.name: Meagan Otieno
guests.bio: VP of Data at a healthtech company, formerly a research scientist. Writes a newsletter on data contracts and pipeline observability read by a few thousand engineers.

guests.name: Tobias Renwick
guests.bio: Staff engineer turned independent consultant specializing in Kubernetes cost optimization. Ran platform for a mid-size ad-tech company through a 4x traffic scale-up.

guests.name: Aiyana Fletcher-Brooks
guests.bio: Co-founder and CTO of a two-sided marketplace startup; previously an early engineer at a well-known payments company. Known for a widely shared essay on postmortem culture.

guests.name: Kwame Osei-Larbi
guests.bio: Engineering manager who has led three separate monolith-to-services migrations. Speaks at conferences about the human side of large refactors.

guests.name: Ines Vandermolen
guests.bio: Security engineer focused on supply-chain attacks against CI pipelines. Formerly on the security team at a large European bank.

guests.name: Rafael Quintero-Diaz
guests.bio: Product manager who moved from consumer social into developer tools. Obsessed with onboarding funnels for technical products.

guests.name: Saoirse Whelan
guests.bio: Distributed systems engineer working on a consensus library used inside two open-source databases. PhD dropout, self-taught the rest.

guests.name: Devendra Bhatt
guests.bio: Founder of a three-year-old observability startup competing against the big three vendors on price and simplicity.

guests.name: Clementine Ashworth
guests.bio: Engineering director who rebuilt her company's incident response process after a 14-hour outage. Now consults on the side.

guests.name: Yusuf Erdogan
guests.bio: Machine learning infrastructure lead, previously built the feature store at a large recommendation-heavy consumer app.

episodes.title: The Golden Path Nobody Follows
episodes.show_notes: Priya walks through why Ledgerway's platform team stopped building 'one true way' tooling and started instrumenting which paths engineers actually took. We get into the political cost of deprecating a beloved internal tool, and why she now measures platform adoption the same way a product team measures activation.

episodes.title: Shipping a Feature Flag Library Solo
episodes.show_notes: Dorian explains the economics of running a three-person devtools studio against VC-backed competitors, and the specific moment he decided to open-source the core and charge only for the dashboard.

episodes.title: Data Contracts Are a People Problem
episodes.show_notes: Meagan makes the case that most data contract failures are organizational, not technical: nobody owns the handoff between the team producing an event and the team consuming it. She shares the escalation ladder Careframe built to fix it.

episodes.title: Cutting a Kubernetes Bill in Half
episodes.show_notes: A practical walkthrough of the four changes that made the biggest dent in a six-figure monthly cloud bill: right-sizing requests, bin-packing with a smarter scheduler, spot instances for batch, and killing zombie namespaces nobody remembered owning.

episodes.title: Postmortems Nobody Reads
episodes.show_notes: Aiyana revisits her viral essay on postmortem culture two years later: what changed at Marketfold, what didn't, and why she now thinks the document format itself is the wrong lever to pull.

episodes.title: Three Monoliths, Three Migrations
episodes.show_notes: Kwame compares three service-extraction projects he has led, and argues that the technical plan matters less than sequencing the migration around a single team's calendar so nobody is mid-cutover during a launch freeze.

episodes.title: Your CI Pipeline Is a Supply Chain
episodes.show_notes: Ines breaks down two real CI compromise techniques she has seen inside client audits, and the boring, unglamorous controls that actually stop them: pinned action SHAs, ephemeral runners, and signed build provenance.

episodes.title: Onboarding a Developer Tool in Under Five Minutes
episodes.show_notes: Rafael dissects Buildhook's onboarding funnel step by step, including the one confusing screen that was quietly costing them a third of signups, and how he found it without a redesign.

episodes.title: Consensus Is the Easy Part
episodes.show_notes: Saoirse argues the hard part of building Quorumkit was never the Raft implementation, it was the operational tooling around leader changes that operators actually needed at 3am.

episodes.title: Underpricing Observability on Purpose
episodes.show_notes: Devendra explains why Tracewell deliberately prices below the big three vendors and how that decision shapes every engineering tradeoff the company makes, down to which storage engine they chose.

episodes.title: The 14-Hour Outage That Rebuilt Our On-Call
episodes.show_notes: A detailed retelling of the outage, the three separate failures that had to line up for it to happen, and the specific staffing and tooling changes Fenwick made afterward.

episodes.title: Building a Feature Store Before It Was a Category
episodes.show_notes: Yusuf traces the feature store he built years before the term existed, and what he'd do differently knowing what the ecosystem looks like today.
